chapter: Leo Watson and the Panassie sessions
title: Leo Watson's scat singing and why no one matched it
summary: Leo started with background fills and grew into original scat solos; Bunn has heard nobody like him, and Eddie Jefferson also called him the greatest.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, it was so personal. You know, like a lot of the other scat singers afterwards, they would copy a solo from a horn player, you know. But his stuff --
He was original.
Yeah. You saw that grow over the years, didn't you.
That's right.
When he first started out he was doing --
And he died out here.
Yeah. Well, like on those early records, like on the Five Cousins records and, you know, the Nephews and Cousins and the early Spirits, he was doing those background fills.
Yeah.
Was that how he started, just doing those backgrounds, and then gradually worked it into a solo.
Yeah.
Did he always do those crazy words
He'd make up -- and stuff? Almost like poems, you know.
That's right. I ain't never heard nobody like it.
Did he used to rap? Like in the clubs, did he used to talk and tell jokes or anything like that?
No.
It was just when the music -- with the music.
Just when that music was playing, he'd do it.
Come a long way from St. Louis, huh?
Yeah. And he died out here, right downtown. God rest his soul. I ain't never heard nobody like that since. And that's been a long time, since, and I'm still here. I never heard nothing like that yet.
Yeah.

That's the God's honest truth. And when scat singing comes up and people start talking about scat singing, I say, 'You ain't got nothing to talk about. Have you ever heard Leo Watson?' 'Well, we heard about him, but I don't know.' You know.
Yeah.
I say, 'Well, I know. I ain't never heard nobody like him.' And here the boy's passed, and I still ain't
heard nothing like him. I know, I was talking to -- did you ever hear of Eddie Jefferson?
I've heard of him.
Yeah. I was talking to him last year, and I mentioned that I was coming out to see you.
Yeah.
And he looked like he'd seen a ghost or something.
Yeah.
He didn't know you were still around, and he mentioned Leo and said he was the greatest.
That's right. And that ain't no lie. I ain't never heard nobody like him. And I'm in my 70s.
